verdict.rationale: LanceDB documents building and managing vector indexes, offers a choice of three quantization types (PQ, RQ, SQ) that compress indexes, and allows forcing an exhaustive flat scan for exact results, which together give some recall/latency/memory trade-off levers. The pack shows no specific tunable index parameters such as HNSW graph settings. Missing for 10: documented HNSW graph parameters (e.g. M/ef), query-time tuning knobs, explicit recall-vs-latency/memory guidance or benchmarks, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can tune index parameters (HNSW graph settings, index types) to trade recall against latency and memory

citations.quote: LanceDB provides $3$ distinct quantization techniques: Product Quantization (PQ), RaBitQ Quantization (RQ), and Scalar Quantization (SQ).
Quantization is used in LanceDB to efficiently compress and store vector indexes.
Force an exhaustive (flat) scan for exact, ground-truth results.
Build and manage LanceDB vector indexes.
